criteria.criterion: Injected Python/native-like hang/crash/OOM/output flood gets classified and bounded
criteria.detail: Real spawned children (never mocks of the supervisor): hang -> status timeout/failure_kind wall with SIGTERM->grace->SIGKILL process-group kill (test_hang_is_bounded_timeout_and_retried_once); SIGTERM-ignoring child escalates to SIGKILL (test_sigterm_ignoring_child_is_killed); real SIGSEGV -> failed/crash with signal name recorded (test_sigsegv_crash_classified_and_retried_once); memory growth -> failed/memory_limit via live RSS probe kill on macOS and RLIMIT_AS inside the child on Linux (test_memory_growth_is_bounded_and_classified); stdout and stderr floods -> failed/output_limit with only bounded head+tail samples retained (test_stdout/stderr_flood_is_bounded_and_classified); nonzero exit -> failed/exit; spawn failure -> failed/spawn_error; leaked same-group descendants are reaped after leader exit (test_leaked_descendant_is_reaped_after_completed_leader, test_hang-grandchild coverage). Committed F20 worker-fault-* fixture scenarios are additionally exercised through tests/fixtures/fault_double.py (TestWorkerFaultFixtures). All bounds enforced by the parent poll loop, never SIGALRM.

Committed report bytes are the child's produced bytes verbatim: tmp-sibling write -> fsync -> os.replace -> directory fsync (atomic_write_bytes); test_identical_runs_produce_byte_identical_reports asserts byte-identical reports across two runs; test_completed_job_commits_report_verbatim compares bytes; resume verifies sha256+config_digest and marks the job skipped without rewriting (test_resume_skips_verified_completed_and_preserves_bytes). A failed/killed sibling job never touches a completed job's committed report (partial-run test).

limits.retries defaults to native.max_retries = 1; only transient kinds (exit, crash, wall, spawn_error) are retryable, each with a fresh worker and fresh scratch, and only while run_wall_seconds leaves room (_retryable). test_retry_is_bounded_to_one asserts attempts stop at 2; test_transient_failure_succeeds_on_single_retry covers the success path; test_run_deadline_preempts_retry asserts no retry past the run deadline. output_limit, memory_limit, missing_output, report_invalid and cancelled are never retried.

A child that exits 0 without declaring an output is a completed job with attempts == 1 and no retry (test_empty_success_is_completed_and_not_retried). An exit-0 child that declared an output it did not produce is failed/missing_output - a deterministic defect that is also never retried (test_missing_declared_output_fails_and_is_not_retried).

criteria.criterion: Ctrl-C terminates descendants and leaves valid partial artifact.
criteria.detail: SIGINT/SIGTERM to the supervisor process (and an in-process request_cancel) forwards to a cancel: every live process group is SIGTERM->SIGKILL terminated including leaked descendants, queued jobs receive terminal 'cancelled' records (I05 - no job left unterminated), and index.json plus journal.jsonl are still written so the partial artifact stays valid (test_sigint_to_driver_kills_process_group_and_keeps_partial via a real driver subprocess; test_in_process_sigint_cancels_run). Run status reports 'cancelled' with per-job counts journaled in run_terminal.

criteria.criterion: One task failure does not poison the whole corpus (I17 containment)
criteria.detail: A crashing/hanging job terminates as failed/timeout while earlier and later jobs still complete and commit reports; run status is 'partial' (mixed) not 'failed' (smoke evidence in commands.log: file-a completed while file-b crashed and file-c timed out). index.json records a terminal record for every planned job.

criteria.criterion: jobs default 1; PDFium/reader calls stay out of concurrent threads
criteria.detail: Limits.jobs defaults to native.default_jobs = 1 (test_default_jobs_is_one). jobs > 1 requires an explicit CPU/RAM-aware ParallelAdmission and is refused otherwise (test_jobs_two_requires_explicit_admission; admitted concurrency verified in test_admitted_parallel_jobs_run_concurrently). The supervisor uses zero threads and zero engine calls: all reader engine calls (pypdfium2, pypdf, tesseract adapters) execute inside child processes only (test_supervision_uses_processes_not_threads scans the module for thread creation), so PDFium is never invoked from concurrent threads (s26).

environment.python: CPython 3.13.15 via uv frozen native/.venv (system python3 is 3.14.7; all runs used the frozen project interpreter)
environment.note: RLIMIT_AS is rejected by macOS; on this host the memory bound is the live libproc RSS probe + post-exit wait4 ru_maxrss. Linux adds in-child RLIMIT_AS and /proc VmRSS probing. rlimit_support is recorded per run in index.json.

limitations: Verified on macOS arm64 only in this worktree; the Linux rlimit path (RLIMIT_AS, /proc RSS) is implemented and probed but awaits the Homebase/Linux verification round.

Memory bound is layered and degraded where the platform refuses rlimits (macOS RLIMIT_AS): the RSS probe polls at 100 ms so a child could briefly exceed the bound before the kill lands; a container remains the hardened route per THREAT_MODEL.
RLIMIT_CPU is only a backstop (wall deadline +60 s); the authoritative deadline is the parent's poll loop.
Unreapable D-state children are recorded as 'abandoned' (journal child_unreaped, job classified) rather than hanging the run forever.
The single native/tests/ocr failure on this host is a T27-owned macOS path-canonicalization issue outside T29 scope; preserved verbatim, not weakened.
Resume refuses a changed per-job config digest (new run directory required) - stricter than silently rerunning, per the byte-stability contract.
